manifest.summary: Added greeting.py (repository root) exposing greeting(name: str) -> str that strips leading/trailing whitespace, returns "Hello, <name>!" with the stripped name substituted literally, returns "Hello, friend!" for blank/whitespace-only names, and preserves Unicode names literally with no normalization/encoding/transliteration; no network or filesystem side effects. Added tests/test_greeting.py with a standard-library-only unittest suite covering a normal name, leading/trailing whitespace trimming, blank and whitespace-only friend cases, and literal Unicode preservation. Appended an additive README.md section documenting the module and including the exact command python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v; all pre-existing content unchanged (README diff is 19 insertions, 0 deletions; no .github/workflows exists or was touched; no credentials or private execution history introduced). Verified: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v runs green (6 tests OK). Committed as a single clean commit on top of the existing ancestry.

Implemented the review rework (feedback 0bd0380c-dc9d-4ec7-af0f-19158f729324) in the managed worktree (ws_9385294369445e6c3d9a8a7d7ee93af7cd8569bb96e949bcbdb60fcd23384894) on top of the previous finalized state (commit 1cdb6f6), committed as dd3303f. Changed only tests/test_greeting.py (+40/-3): (1) replaced test_no_network_or_filesystem_side_effects with a meaningful guard that swaps builtins.open and socket.socket for functions raising AssertionError, so the test fails if greeting() attempts filesystem or network I/O (verified by poisoning greeting() with open() and socket.socket() in a sandbox: both produced the guard's AssertionError and a failing test); (2) added test_unicode_surrounding_whitespace_is_trimmed covering U+00A0 and U+3000 trimmed while the Unicode name is preserved; (3) added test_decomposed_unicode_name_is_preserved_literally asserting NFD 'Jose\u0301' is returned with exact code points and not normalized to composed 'José'; also extended the whitespace-only case with '\u00a0\u3000'. greeting.py, README.md (additive section with the literal command 'python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v' at line 20) and all other pre-existing files are unchanged; no .github/workflows exists in this repo and none was added. Ran the exact documented command from the repository root on Python 3.13.5: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v -> Ran 8 tests, OK, exit 0, using only the standard library. Working tree is clean; no credentials or private history published; no network/filesystem side effects in the function.

Added the Python 3 greeting module to the repository root per Specification: greeting.py exposes greeting(name: str) -> str which strips leading/trailing whitespace, returns "Hello, <name>!" with the stripped name substituted literally for nonempty results, returns "Hello, friend!" for blank/whitespace-only names, and preserves Unicode names literally (no normalization, encoding conversion, or transliteration); the function is pure with no network/filesystem side effects. Added tests/test_greeting.py, a standard-library-only (unittest) suite covering a normal name, leading/trailing whitespace trimming, blank and whitespace-only friend cases, and Unicode names preserved literally. README.md gained an additive '## greeting module' section (existing content unchanged) that documents the module and includes the exact command `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v`. Verified: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v runs green (6 tests, OK, exit 0) on Python 3.13.5 using only the standard library; git diff vs base aa274b4 shows only README.md (additive), greeting.py (new), tests/test_greeting.py (new); no .github/workflows exists in the base or was touched; all pre-existing files (probe files, owner-delivery-synthetic-proof.txt, uncertain file, original README lines) remain byte-for-byte unchanged; worktree finalized clean with no uncommitted changes.
